question: What was Kinsale Capital Group's 2025 combined ratio for its Commercial Property division?
grading: Must state that Kinsale does not disclose a combined ratio (or loss/expense ratio) for the Commercial Property division; it reports one segment and only company-wide ratios. May add the consolidated FY2025 combined ratio 75.9% (loss ratio 55.1%, expense ratio 20.8%) clearly labelled consolidated, and the division-level data that is disclosed (Commercial Property gross written premiums USD 374.5M, -17.9% y/y, 18.9% of total). Fail if any division-level combined-ratio number is presented as company-reported, or if 75.9% is presented as the Commercial Property ratio.
answer: Kinsale does not disclose a combined ratio for the Commercial Property division. The company has one reportable segment (Excess and Surplus Lines Insurance) and reports loss, expense and combined ratios only on a consolidated basis: FY2025 combined ratio 75.9% (loss ratio 55.1%, expense ratio 20.8%) [H15-E1][H15-E2]. By division it discloses gross written premiums only; Commercial Property GWP was USD 374.5 million in 2025 (18.9% of total, down 17.9% from USD 456.2 million) [H15-E1]. A text search of the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 Q1/Q2 10-Qs, the Q4 2025 and 2026 Q1/Q2 earnings releases and the January 8, 2026 Investor Day slide text finds no combined or loss ratio tied to a named division [H15-E1][H15-E3][H15-E4].

output.answer:
**Kinsale does not disclose a combined ratio for its Commercial Property Division — that figure does not exist in the company's public reporting.**

**Why:** Kinsale Capital reports as a **single reportable segment** ("Excess and Surplus Lines Insurance"). Its 10-K/10-Q filings state: "The Company has one reportable segment, the Excess and Surplus Lines Insurance segment... The Company reports operating and financial results in a single segment." (Commercial Property is one of several *underwriting divisions* — alongside Excess Casualty, General Casualty, Small Business Casualty, Construction, Allied Health, Products Liability, etc. — but divisions are not reporting segments.) Loss, expense, and combined ratios are disclosed only on a consolidated company-wide basis.

**What is available for reference (company-wide, 2025):**
- **Full-year 2025 combined ratio: 75.9%** (loss ratio 55.1%, expense ratio 20.8%)
- Q4 2025 combined ratio: 71.7%
- 2024 full-year combined ratio: 76.4%

**The Commercial Property Division's actual disclosed metric** is premium volume, not profitability. Gross written premiums in the division fell sharply in 2025 (~18%) and further in early 2026 (−28.3% in Q1 2026; −32.7% in Q2 2026) due to heightened competition and rate decreases. Excluding Commercial Property, gross written premiums grew ~13–18% in 2025.

Sources:
- [Kinsale 2025 Q4/Year-End Results](https://ir.kinsalecapitalgroup.com/news/news-details/2026/Kinsale-Capital-Group-Inc--Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-Results/default.aspx)
- [Kinsale Q1 2026 Results](https://ir.kinsalecapitalgroup.com/news/news-details/2026/Kinsale-Capital-Group-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)
- [Kinsale 10-Q (segment note)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1669162/000166916226000026/knsl-20260331.htm)

If you saw a specific "Commercial Property combined ratio" figure somewhere, it's likely an analyst estimate or a third-party construct — Kinsale itself does not publish it.
